covers.quote: Report them in the body of the text instead.

rules.quote: Don’t create a table for only one or 2 items.
rules.violation_condition: a table created containing only one or two data items
rules.why: Clear negative prohibition on table size; advice on alternative absorbed per G-4.

rules.quote: Don’t make tables with other tables inside them (known as ‘nested’tables).
rules.violation_condition: a table containing another table nested inside it
rules.why: Direct structural prohibition on nested tables.

covers.quote: a title (also called a caption)
row and column headings
information (entries)
a cross-reference in the text.

rules.quote: You must give a table:
rules.violation_condition: a table lacking a title (caption), row or column headings, entries, or a cross-reference in the text
rules.why: G-2 combines list elements into one compound requirement for mandatory table components.

covers.quote: Don’t use colour as the only way to convey meaning.

rules.quote: Don’t rely on colour as the only visual means of conveying information in tables.
rules.violation_condition: information in a table conveyed solely by colour without an alternative visual indicator or text
rules.why: WCAG requirement on colour dependency, restated in later section; consolidated per G-4.

rules.quote: Don’t leave cells empty. Use ‘zero’ or ‘nil’ or 'n/a' where there is no data. If it is numeric data, use the numeric zero (0). Only use zero if that is the true value.
rules.violation_condition: an empty table cell, or using '0' when 0 is not the true value
when: Use 'zero' or 'nil' or 'n/a' where there is no data.
If it is numeric data, use the numeric zero (0).
Only use zero if that is the true value.
rules.why: Prohibits empty cells in tables and specifies allowable fallback strings (G-2).

covers.quote: You must still refer to the table in the body of the text.

rules.quote: It is essential to refer to a table in the text.
rules.violation_condition: a table in a document that is not referred to anywhere in the surrounding text
rules.why: Core requirement to reference all tables in the body text (G-4).

covers.quote: A single table on a webpage does not need a table number.

rules.quote: If you use tables repeatedly, number tables and include the table number when you refer to the table in the text.
rules.violation_condition: un-numbered tables or table references lacking table numbers in a document with multiple tables
when: Applies when a document uses tables repeatedly.
A single table on a webpage does not need a table number.
rules.why: G-2 and G-3 combine rule with single-table exception.

rules.quote: Ensure that the table number referenced in the text matches the table number in the title.
rules.violation_condition: a mismatch between the table number cited in the body text and the table number in the table's title
rules.why: Specific cross-referencing consistency rule.

examples.note: Refers to table number without repeating full title

parts.quote: Table 2 shows that average rainfall has …
Table 2 (Average monthly rainfall, June 2017 to December 2019) shows that average rainfall has …

rules.quote: Don’t repeat the whole title of the table in the text.
rules.violation_condition: a text reference to a table that repeats the full title of the table
rules.why: Direct rule accompanied by Write/Don't write examples.

rules.quote: Don’t refer to ‘the table below’ or ‘the table above’.
rules.violation_condition: referring to a table using relative positional terms like 'the table below' or 'the table above'
rules.why: Clear pattern-matching rule against directional/positional cross-references.

rules.quote: Avoid referring to a page number in the text.
rules.violation_condition: referring to a table by page number in the text
rules.why: Explicit instruction prohibiting page number references.

covers.quote: Use the same grammatical form for each entry in a column.

rules.quote: The text or data in a table should use the same grammatical form (for example, noun, noun phrase or sentence).
rules.specification: Entries within the same column or table should maintain parallel grammatical structure.
rules.violation_condition: inconsistent grammatical forms within a table's entries or columns
rules.why: Parallelism rule for table entries; absorbs 527b8ae629cf per G-4.

rules.quote: Avoid using them in word processing applications.
rules.violation_condition: merged cells present in tables within word processing applications
when: In word processing applications (merged cells can be made accessible in HTML and PDF).
rules.why: Clear condition and prohibition on merged cells.

covers.quote: the first row contains the column headings
the first column (also known as the ‘stub’) contains the row headings.

rules.quote: Structure tables so:
rules.violation_condition: a table where the first row does not contain column headings or the first column does not contain row headings
rules.why: Prescribes standard table header structure (G-2).

rules.quote: Mark up tables to show header cells and data cells.
rules.violation_condition: table markup lacking distinct header cells (e.g. <th>) and data cells (<td>)
rules.why: Accessibility requirement for semantic table tagging.

rules.quote: If you use a complex table, you must define the column and row groups and mark up the table accordingly.
rules.violation_condition: a complex table with header cells spanning multiple rows/columns that lacks column and row group markup
when: Applies to complex tables with header cells spanning more than one column or row.
rules.why: Mandatory WCAG accessibility requirement for complex tables.

covers.quote: column headings appear at the top of each page
you repeat row headings on each page.

rules.quote: If a table runs over pages when printed, ensure:
rules.violation_condition: a multi-page printed table that does not repeat column headings at the top of each page or row headings on each page
when: When a table runs over pages in print.
rules.why: Specific print pagination requirement for repeating headers (G-2).

rules.quote: Don’t include this information in the table title or caption or in ordinary footnotes or endnotes.
rules.violation_condition: table notes or source citations placed in the table title/caption or ordinary footnotes/endnotes rather than in notes below the table
rules.why: Prohibition on placing table notes/sources inside caption or standard footnotes.

covers.quote: To connect the note under the table to the information it refers to in the table use:
a symbol such as an asterisk (*) or hash (#) for only one note
superscript numbers or letters for more than one note.

rules.quote: Use only one type of note in a table. Either use all symbols, all superscript numbers or all superscript letters.
rules.violation_condition: mixing symbols, superscript numbers, and superscript letters within the same table's notes
rules.why: Defines rules for note locators and forbids mixing notation types (G-2).

covers.quote: abbreviations
notes to superscript locators
general note to the table
source of data (use the appropriate form for author–date or documentary–note).

rules.quote: When writing table notes, list them in the following order:
rules.violation_condition: table notes listed out of the specified order (abbreviations, then notes to superscript locators, then general note, then source)
rules.why: Strict ordering requirement for table notes (G-2).

rules.quote: Align notes to the left. They should not extend beyond the edges of the table. Don’t use superscript for the note identifiers (the symbol, number or letter) in the note. They should be the same font size as the text of the notes so that they are easily found.
rules.violation_condition: table notes not left-aligned, extending beyond table edges, or using superscript identifiers in the note text
rules.why: Formatting specification for table notes consolidated per G-2.

covers.quote: Align text to the left.
Align numbers to the right.

rules.quote: In general:
rules.violation_condition: table text not left-aligned, or numbers not right-aligned
rules.why: Standard alignment rules for text and numeric columns (G-2).

rules.quote: In addition, decimal points in the column should line up.
rules.violation_condition: decimal points within a numeric column not aligned
rules.why: Specific alignment requirement for decimal figures.

rules.quote: Text should be set horizontally so it is easy to read. Don’t rotate text to display vertically.
rules.violation_condition: text set vertically or rotated in a table
rules.why: Direct prohibition against vertical/rotated text in tables.

covers.quote: Align column headings with the content in the column.
Include the unit in the heading if it is not in the title or caption.
Left-align row headings.

rules.quote: For column and row headings:
rules.violation_condition: column headings not aligned with column content, unit omitted from heading when not in caption, or row headings not left-aligned
rules.why: Formatting and labeling rules for column and row headings (G-2).

rules.quote: Don’t use a point size that is too small. Although typefaces and sizes vary, anything smaller than 8 points is too small.
rules.violation_condition: table text set at a font size smaller than 8 points
when: In print publications.
rules.why: Explicit minimum threshold of 8pt for print tables.

covers.quote: omit the rule at the bottom of the table – this is a visual cue that the table is not complete
at the bottom of the table, insert ‘(continued)’ aligned right to the edge of the table
on the next page, repeat the caption and insert ‘(continued)’ after the table number – for example, ‘Table 3 (continued): Farm output from 1990 to 2000’.

rules.quote: Try to keep tables on one page. If you must use a long table:
rules.violation_condition: a multi-page table in print failing to omit bottom rule on intermediate pages, missing right-aligned '(continued)' at bottom, or missing '(continued)' in repeated caption
when: Applies when a table runs over more than one page in print.
rules.why: Compound print continuation styling rules (G-2).

rules.quote: Don’t use cell or text formatting to convey meaning. It can make the table difficult to read. Screen reader users cannot ‘see’ the formatting.
rules.violation_condition: using cell or text styling/formatting (such as bold or shading) as the sole means of conveying meaning in a table
rules.why: Accessibility requirement barring purely typographic/visual formatting to convey semantic meaning.

rules.quote: Use the same font, and font sizes, rule (line) thicknesses and colour schemes for tables throughout the document.
rules.violation_condition: inconsistent fonts, font sizes, rule thicknesses, or colour schemes between tables in the same document
rules.why: Document-wide table styling consistency rule.

covers.quote: Provide a summary for complex tables
The summary does not provide the same information as the title or caption.

rules.quote: For complex tables, provide a summary to give people who use screen readers an overview of the information in the table.
rules.violation_condition: a complex table lacking an accessible summary attribute or element
when: Applies to complex tables.
rules.why: WCAG requirement for table summaries on complex structures (G-1, G-2).
